components.note: 发 is the simplified form of 發, which pictured two hands drawing back a bow and releasing an arrow — the sense of something launching or sending outward is preserved in meanings like 发音 'to emit a sound.'
立 here depicts a tongue positioned to speak.
日 here depicts an open mouth — a tongue forming sound in the mouth gave 音 its meaning 'sound, tone.'

example.hanzi: 学生们努力练习正确的发音。
example.pinyin: xuéshengmen nǔlì liànxí zhèngquè de fāyīn.
example.english: The students work hard to practice correct pronunciation.
example.fact: The human vocal folds vibrate somewhere between 100 and 1,000 times per second to generate the raw pitch behind speech, and it's the vocal tract's shaping of that airflow — the tongue, teeth, and lips working together — that turns vibration into recognizable words. Songbirds do something similar with a specialized organ called a syrinx, which lets them produce two independent pitches at once, something no human vocal tract can manage.

components.note: 穴 (hole) — 窃 originally described sneaking through a hole to steal.
切 (qiè) gives the sound — an exact match with 窃.
口 (mouth) — words spoken by a mouth are what reach the ear, giving 听 its meaning 'to listen.'
斤 stands in for the ear in this simplified character — the target that spoken words reach.
口 (a vessel), shown four times — a set of cooking vessels.
犬 (a dog) — guarding the vessels, the source of 器's meaning 'vessel, tool, instrument.'

example.hanzi: 警方在办公室里发现了一个窃听器。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng zài bàngōngshì lǐ fāxiàn le yí gè qiètīngqì.
example.english: Police discovered a bug in the office.
example.fact: In 1945, Soviet schoolchildren gave the US ambassador in Moscow a carved wooden Great Seal of the United States as a gift of friendship; hidden inside was a passive listening device — nicknamed "The Thing" — that needed no battery or wiring and went undetected for seven years, quietly relaying conversations from the ambassador's own study.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — 联 originally meant 'connected, linked,' perhaps through the image of joined loops.
关 (guān) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from lián.
合 pictures 亼 (a lid) fitting down over 口 (a container's mouth) — two parts closing together perfectly, the image behind its meaning 'to combine, to unite.'
囗 (a boundary/enclosure) surrounding 玉 (jade, treasure) — a country pictured as protected, valuable territory.

example.hanzi: 联合国总部设在纽约市。
example.pinyin: Liánhéguó zǒngbù shè zài Niǔyuē Shì.
example.english: The United Nations headquarters is located in New York City.
example.fact: The United Nations was founded in San Francisco in 1945 by 51 countries in the aftermath of World War II. Its Manhattan headquarters sits on land purchased with an $8.5 million donation from John D. Rockefeller Jr., and the site is technically international territory rather than part of the United States.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.
犭 (dog) shows 猎 relates to hunting with animals.
昔 (xī) gives a sound distantly related to liè, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 爸爸小时候常常跟爷爷一起去打猎。
example.pinyin: bàba xiǎo shíhou chángcháng gēn yéye yìqǐ qù dǎliè.
example.english: When Dad was young, he often went hunting with Grandpa.
example.fact: Long before the bow and arrow, ancient hunters used a tool called an atlatl — a spear-thrower with a notched handle — to nearly double the speed and range of a thrown dart. Some atlatl-launched projectiles could travel over 100 meters, and the technology appears independently in hunting cultures across the Americas, Australia, and Europe going back at least 20,000 years.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 渡 describes crossing over a body of water.
度 (dù) gives the sound — an exact match with 渡.
辶 (to walk/move) — shows 过's core meaning of 'passing through' or 'crossing'
咼 (guō) gives a sound close to 过's reading guò; the simplified form 过 now uses 寸 in place of 咼, but the phonetic connection traces back to the traditional character 過

example.hanzi: 他们乘小船渡过了那条河。
example.pinyin: tāmen chéng xiǎochuán dùguò le nà tiáo hé.
example.english: They crossed that river by small boat.
example.fact: In 49 BC, Julius Caesar led his army across the Rubicon River, a shallow stream in northern Italy, defying Roman law that forbade a general from bringing troops into Italy proper. The crossing triggered a civil war and gave rise to the modern idiom "crossing the Rubicon" for passing a point of no return.

meanings: (of a liquid or gas) to leak

components.note: 氵 (water) — leaking is described using the water radical, whether literal or figurative.
世 (shì) gives a sound distantly related to xiè, having drifted apart over time.
氵 (water) — 漏 describes water escaping through a gap.
屚 pictures rain seeping in through a roof, the image behind 漏's meaning 'to leak.'

example.hanzi: 那家工厂发生了化学品泄漏事故。
example.pinyin: nà jiā gōngchǎng fāshēng le huàxuépǐn xièlòu shìgù.
example.english: That factory had a chemical leak accident.
example.fact: The 2010 Deepwater Horizon disaster in the Gulf of Mexico released an estimated 4.9 million barrels of oil over 87 days before the well was capped, making it the largest accidental marine oil spill in history. Engineers eventually stopped the leak using a specially designed capping stack lowered more than a mile to the seafloor.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 怪 relates to an inner feeling of unease or surprise at something odd.
The right-hand side, a simplified form of 圣, once depicted a hand shaping earth — repurposed here mainly for its shape, leaving 怪 to mean 'strange' or 'to blame.'
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
寸 (a hand) reaching for 旦 (originally 貝, a shell used as currency) — a picture of grasping something valuable, hence 'to obtain, to get.'

example.hanzi: 怪不得今天这么冷，原来下雪了。
example.pinyin: guàibude jīntiān zhème lěng, yuánlái xià xuě le.
example.english: No wonder it's so cold today — it's actually snowing.
example.fact: Snow forms only when the atmosphere is cold enough for ice crystals to grow around microscopic dust or pollen particles high in the clouds; if the air near the ground warms even slightly above freezing on the way down, the flakes melt into rain instead. Each snowflake's six-sided symmetry comes from the hexagonal way water molecules bond as they freeze.

components.note: 阝 (a hill/place) — 陆 relates to solid ground, as opposed to water
击 (jī) gives a sound distantly related to 陆's reading lù, having drifted apart considerably over time
戈 (a dagger-axe, a weapon) — 战 relates to fighting and war.
占 (zhàn) gives the sound — 战 is also pronounced zhàn, an exact match.
阝 (a mound or place) — 队 pictures people gathering together.
人 (person) — people gathering in one place gave 队 its meaning 'a team' or 'a line/queue.'

example.hanzi: 他退伍前是海军陆战队的一名军官。
example.pinyin: tā tuìwǔ qián shì hǎijūn lùzhànduì de yì míng jūnguān.
example.english: Before he left the service, he was an officer in the marine corps.
example.fact: The United States Marine Corps traces its founding to November 10, 1775, when the Second Continental Congress authorized two battalions of Marines to serve aboard Navy ships. That founding date is still celebrated annually as the Marine Corps' birthday, making it one of the oldest continuously operating military branches in the country.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 洗 describes cleaning something with water.
先 (xiān) shares the initial x- with xǐ, though the rhyme has drifted.
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.hanzi: 吃饭前记得洗手。
example.pinyin: chīfàn qián jìde xǐshǒu.
example.english: Remember to wash your hands before eating.
example.fact: In 1847, Hungarian physician Ignaz Semmelweis noticed that maternity ward deaths from childbed fever dropped sharply after he required doctors to wash their hands with a chlorinated lime solution between autopsies and patient exams. His findings were ridiculed by the medical establishment of the time, and it took decades — after germ theory was widely accepted — for handwashing to become standard practice.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 海 relates to bodies of water, specifically the sea.
每 (měi) gives a hint of the sound — 海 is pronounced hǎi, a connection that has shifted over time.
辶 (to walk/move) — 选 relates to the process of selecting, as if moving through options
先 (xiān) gives a sound close to 选's reading xuǎn

example.hanzi: 这次歌唱比赛先进行海选，再决出决赛选手。
example.pinyin: zhè cì gēchàng bǐsài xiān jìnxíng hǎixuǎn, zài juéchū juésài xuǎnshǒu.
example.english: This singing competition starts with an open audition before the finalists are decided.
example.fact: Many corals and reef fish reproduce through mass spawning events, releasing millions of eggs and sperm into the water at once during a single synchronized night each year, often timed to the lunar cycle. Broadcasting so many gametes into the open ocean compensates for the fact that only a tiny fraction will ever meet and survive.

components.note: 丿 (something falling) — an object slipping away.
夫 (a hand/person) — the object slipping out of a hand, giving 失 its meaning 'to lose.'
巾 (cloth) — 常 originally referred to a long skirt or banner made of cloth, later coming to mean something 'usual' or 'ordinary.'
尚 (shàng) gives a hint of the sound — 常 is pronounced cháng, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 最近他的行为有些失常。
example.pinyin: zuìjìn tā de xíngwéi yǒuxiē shīcháng.
example.english: His behavior has been a bit abnormal lately.
example.fact: El Niño is an irregular, naturally occurring disruption of normal ocean-atmosphere patterns in which surface waters in the eastern Pacific warm several degrees above average, altering weather worldwide. It recurs every two to seven years without a fixed schedule, which is part of why forecasting its onset and strength remains genuinely difficult even with modern satellite data.

components.note: 立 here depicts a tongue positioned to speak.
日 here depicts an open mouth — a tongue forming sound in the mouth gave 音 its meaning 'sound, tone.'
乐 is the simplified form of 樂, which depicted a wooden 木 instrument strung with strings 幺, played with a pick 白 — music came to represent joy, giving 乐 its meaning 'happy, music.'
刂 (knife) contributes to the character's form, though its link to 剧's meaning 'drama' has faded over time.
居 (jū) gives a rhyme close to jù, with the tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 我们周末去百老汇看了一场音乐剧。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zhōumò qù Bǎilǎohuì kàn le yì chǎng yīnyuèjù.
example.english: We went to see a musical on Broadway this weekend.
example.fact: "The Phantom of the Opera" opened on Broadway in 1988 and ran continuously for 35 years before closing in April 2023, racking up more than 13,500 performances — the longest run in Broadway history. Its original production reportedly grossed over one billion dollars in New York alone.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 推 relates to pushing something with the hand
隹 (zhuī) gives a loose sound connection to 推's reading tuī
辶 (to walk) — 进 relates to advancing or entering, both movement-related.
井 (jǐng) gives a close sound cue — 进 is pronounced jìn, sharing similar consonant and vowel sounds.

example.hanzi: 新技术大大推进了这个项目的进度。
example.pinyin: xīn jìshù dàdà tuījìn le zhège xiàngmù de jìndù.
example.english: The new technology greatly advanced the project's progress.
example.fact: A rocket engine propels itself forward by Newton's third law: expelling exhaust gas backward at high speed generates an equal and opposite thrust forward, working even in the vacuum of space where there's no air to push against. The Saturn V rocket's first stage burned roughly 15 tons of fuel per second to generate enough thrust to lift itself off the launch pad.

components.note: 鬲 (an ancient three-legged cauldron) — 融 originally described steam rising from a cooking pot as it heated, i.e. melting or blending.
虫 (chóng) gives a sound distantly related to róng, having drifted apart over time.
亻 depicts a person standing upright.
The mirrored stroke beside it shows the same person turned around or reversed — one form changing into another, the image behind 化's meaning 'to transform, to change.'

example.hanzi: 太阳出来后，雪很快就融化了。
example.pinyin: tàiyáng chūlái hòu, xuě hěn kuài jiù rónghuà le.
example.english: After the sun came out, the snow melted quickly.
example.fact: Arctic sea ice has been shrinking at a rate of roughly 13 percent per decade since satellite records began in 1979, with the region's summer minimum extent now less than half of what it was forty years ago. Because darker open ocean water absorbs more sunlight than reflective ice, the melting accelerates further warming in a feedback loop scientists call Arctic amplification.

components.note: 门 is a picture of a double-leafed door or gate, drawn symmetrically to show two swinging panels.
夕 (evening, night) — divination was traditionally done in the evening.
卜 (to divine, reading cracks in bone or shell) — combined with 夕 (evening), an evening divination was for unusual or 'outside' matters, giving 外 its meaning of 'outside' or 'foreign.'

example.hanzi: 有人在门外等你。
example.pinyin: yǒu rén zài ménwài děng nǐ.
example.english: Someone is waiting for you outside the door.
example.fact: The oldest known wooden door in Europe, unearthed near Zurich, Switzerland, dates back to around 3400 BC and was preserved for millennia in waterlogged lakeside soil. It still has visible tool marks from its construction, offering rare direct evidence of Neolithic carpentry.

components.note: 止 (a foot) originally sat above 舟 (a boat).
A foot stepping aboard a boat and moving onward gave 前 its meaning 'ahead, forward, front,' with the boat shape later simplified beyond recognition.

方 is traditionally read as a picture of an ancient plow with a handle and crossbar — a tool that cuts a straight, well-defined line through soil, which may be why the character came to mean 'square, direction, and side.'

example.hanzi: 前方路况不好，请小心驾驶。
example.pinyin: qiánfāng lùkuàng bù hǎo, qǐng xiǎoxīn jiàshǐ.
example.english: Road conditions ahead are poor, please drive carefully.
example.fact: Modern car radar can detect obstacles hundreds of meters ahead by bouncing radio waves off objects and timing their return, the same basic principle used in the earliest air-defense radar systems developed in Britain in the 1930s. Today's automatic emergency braking systems use this to react to a hazard ahead in a fraction of a second — far faster than human reflexes allow.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 伤 describes an injury done to a person's body.
The remaining strokes are a simplified trace of 傷's original right-hand side, which pictured an arrow striking flesh — the source of 伤's meaning 'wound, injury.'
疒 (sickness) — 疤 (a scar) is a mark left by injury, grouped with sickness-related characters.
巴 (bā) gives the sound — an exact match with 疤's reading.

example.hanzi: 他手臂上有一道很深的伤疤。
example.pinyin: tā shǒubì shàng yǒu yì dào hěn shēn de shāngbā.
example.english: There's a deep scar on his arm.
example.fact: Scar tissue forms when the skin's collagen fibers, which normally weave in a random basket-like pattern, instead line up in parallel bundles during rapid wound repair. That different arrangement is why scars look and feel distinct from surrounding skin and never regrow hair follicles or sweat glands.

components.note: 鱼 (fish, broadened to aquatic creatures) — 鳄 names crocodiles and alligators.
咢 (è) gives the sound — an exact match with 鳄's reading.
鱼 is a simplified picture of a fish — the top traces its head and fins, and the strokes below represent its body and tail.

example.hanzi: 河里有一条鳄鱼在晒太阳。
example.pinyin: hé lǐ yǒu yì tiáo èyú zài shài tàiyáng.
example.english: There's a crocodile sunbathing in the river.
example.fact: American alligators can go through as many as 3,000 to 4,000 teeth over a lifetime, constantly replacing worn or lost ones with new teeth growing in beneath the old — a capability scientists have studied for clues about regenerating human dental tissue. Their bite force, meanwhile, is among the strongest measured in any living animal, while the muscles that open their jaws are comparatively weak.

components.note: A drawing of a hand peeling the hide away from an animal.
巾 (cloth) — the bottom half of a belt, hanging straight down.
Above the cloth, the strokes crease as if folded at the waist — depicting a belt or sash, the source of 带's meaning 'belt, band,' later 'to bring, carry along.'

example.hanzi: 他的皮带上有一个金属扣。
example.pinyin: tā de pídài shàng yǒu yí gè jīnshǔ kòu.
example.english: There's a metal buckle on his belt.
example.fact: During the early Industrial Revolution, factories often ran on a single large steam engine that drove one central rotating shaft running the length of the building, with long leather belts looping down to power each individual machine. This "belt and pulley" system meant that if the main engine stopped, every machine in the factory stopped with it.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/city) — represents a place being traveled to.
迶 depicts walking or moving along a path — following someone to the city gave 随 its meaning 'to follow, along with.'
身 depicts a person's torso, originally showing a pregnant woman's body — later broadened to mean 'the body' in general.

example.hanzi: 出门时她总是随身带着一把雨伞。
example.pinyin: chūmén shí tā zǒngshì suíshēn dài zhe yì bǎ yǔsǎn.
example.english: She always carries an umbrella with her when she goes out.
example.fact: Sony's 1979 Walkman was one of the first devices to make truly personal, portable audio possible, letting people carry music with them wherever they went instead of being tied to a stationary stereo. It sold over 200 million units worldwide across its various models before production finally ended in 2010.

components.note: 士 depicts a scholar or gentleman.
口 (mouth) — the words of a wise, respected person were seen as auspicious, giving 吉 its meaning 'lucky, good.'
米 depicts scattered grains of husked rice around a central stalk — a simple picture giving 米 its meaning 'rice, grain.'

example.hanzi: 我的邻居吉米每天早上都去跑步。
example.pinyin: wǒ de línjū Jímǐ měi tiān zǎoshang dōu qù pǎobù.
example.english: My neighbor Jimmy goes running every morning.
example.fact: Jimmy Carter, the 39th President of the United States, left office in 1981 but went on to found the Carter Center and spend decades on humanitarian work, including election monitoring and public health campaigns in dozens of countries. In 2002, he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for those post-presidency efforts.

components.note: 奉 pictures a plant or gift held up between two hands raised together — an offering presented respectfully with both hands, the source of 奉's meaning 'to offer respectfully, to present.'
犬 (dog) — 献 originally referred to offering a dog in sacrifice, extended to mean 'to offer, present.'
南 (nán) gives a sound distantly related to xiàn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 她把一生都奉献给了科学研究。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ yìshēng dōu fèngxiàn gěi le kēxué yánjiū.
example.english: She dedicated her whole life to scientific research.
example.fact: Marie Curie donated the prize money from her first Nobel Prize to scientific research rather than keeping it, and she and her husband deliberately chose not to patent their process for isolating radium so other scientists could use it freely. She died in 1934 of aplastic anemia, almost certainly caused by decades of unprotected exposure to the radioactive materials she studied.

components.note: Strength — force is used to take something.
Gives the sound qù, related to jié but drifted apart over time.
扌 (hand) — relates directly to 持's meaning 'to hold, maintain.'
寺 (sì) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from chí.

example.hanzi: 那架飞机在飞行途中被劫持了。
example.pinyin: nà jià fēijī zài fēixíng túzhōng bèi jiéchí le.
example.english: That plane was hijacked mid-flight.
example.fact: In November 1971, a man using the alias D.B. Cooper hijacked a Boeing 727, demanded $200,000 in ransom, and parachuted out of the plane over the Pacific Northwest — and was never identified or found. The FBI officially closed the unsolved case in 2016, and only a small portion of the ransom cash, found years later along a riverbank, was ever recovered.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 场 relates to a flat open area of ground, such as a field or venue.
昜 (yáng) gives a hint of the sound — 场 is pronounced chǎng, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.
户 (door) — 所 evokes a location or place, such as where a door stands.
斤 (axe) — combined with 户 (door), the image of an axe at a door gave rise to the abstract sense of 'a place' or 'that which.'

example.hanzi: 图书馆是一个安静的学习场所。
example.pinyin: túshūguǎn shì yí gè ānjìng de xuéxí chǎngsuǒ.
example.english: The library is a quiet place to study.
example.fact: Before satellite navigation, pinpointing an exact location at sea depended on knowing accurate time: British clockmaker John Harrison spent decades in the 1700s perfecting a marine chronometer precise enough to determine longitude by comparing local noon to a fixed reference time, finally solving a problem that had cost thousands of sailors' lives to shipwreck.

components.note: 车 (cart) — relates to 转's meaning 'to turn, change direction,' like a wheel turning.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 转 is pronounced zhuǎn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
扌 (hand) — 换 describes an action done by hand, such as swapping or exchanging.
奂 (huàn) gives the sound — an exact match with 换.

example.hanzi: 这个软件可以把文件转换成不同的格式。
example.pinyin: zhège ruǎnjiàn kěyǐ bǎ wénjiàn zhuǎnhuàn chéng bùtóng de géshì.
example.english: This software can convert files into different formats.
example.fact: Hoover Dam converts the gravitational potential energy of water held behind it into electricity by letting the water fall roughly 180 meters through turbines, spinning generators that once supplied enough power for the entire Las Vegas region. Hydropower remains one of the most efficient energy conversion methods known, often exceeding 90 percent efficiency from moving water to electrical output.

components.note: 礻 (spirit/altar) — ancestor worship at a family altar ties 祖 to the spirit radical.
且 (qiě) gives a sound distantly related to zǔ, having drifted apart over time.
囗 (a boundary/enclosure) surrounding 玉 (jade, treasure) — a country pictured as protected, valuable territory.

example.hanzi: 他常常给远在祖国的家人写信。
example.pinyin: tā chángcháng gěi yuǎn zài zǔguó de jiārén xiě xìn.
example.english: He often writes letters to his family far away in his homeland.
example.fact: Russia, often called the "motherland" in its own patriotic tradition, is the largest country on Earth by land area, spanning eleven time zones and covering more than one-eighth of the planet's inhabited land. It stretches so far that when it's morning in its westernmost city, it's already nighttime on its eastern edge.

components.note: 冖 here is a distorted form of 力 (strength) — a simplified way of showing soldiers grouped together.
车 (cart/vehicle) — 军 originally pictured soldiers riding out to battle in war chariots.
才 (talent) — many talented people.
囗 (an enclosure) — gathered together in one place, giving 团 its meaning 'group, team; round, ball-shaped.'

example.hanzi: 罗马军团曾征服了大片欧洲土地。
example.pinyin: Luómǎ jūntuán céng zhēngfú le dà piàn Ōuzhōu tǔdì.
example.english: Roman legions once conquered vast stretches of European territory.
example.fact: A standard Roman legion in the early imperial period numbered around 5,000 soldiers, organized into ten cohorts and further divided into smaller units called centuries — despite the name, typically about 80 men rather than a literal 100. At its height, the Roman Empire maintained roughly 30 legions simultaneously stationed across three continents.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — held in a hand, the image behind 布's meaning 'cloth' and, by extension, 'to spread out, distribute.'
月 (moon) — 朗 describes the moon's bright, clear light.
良 (liáng) gives a rhyme close to lǎng, with a different initial.

example.hanzi: 布朗先生是这所学校的新校长。
example.pinyin: Bùlǎng xiānsheng shì zhè suǒ xuéxiào de xīn xiàozhǎng.
example.english: Mr. Brown is the new principal of this school.
example.fact: In 1827, Scottish botanist Robert Brown observed pollen grains suspended in water jittering constantly under his microscope for no apparent reason. That erratic motion, later named Brownian motion after him, wasn't fully explained until 1905, when Albert Einstein showed it was caused by countless collisions with individual water molecules — providing some of the first solid evidence that atoms and molecules actually exist.

components.note: 八 here depicts something splitting apart or being divided.
厶 is an old form meaning 'private' or 'one's own' — 公 shows dividing up private property to share it fairly, giving rise to the meaning 'public' or 'fair.'

事 is thought to depict a hand holding a forked tool once used by scribes and officials to record events — the source of its meaning 'affair, matter,' and a shape closely related to 史 (history) and 吏 (official).

example.hanzi: 他这次来纯粹是为了公事。
example.pinyin: tā zhè cì lái chúncuì shì wèile gōngshì.
example.english: This time he came purely for official business.
example.fact: China's imperial civil service examination system, which selected government officials based on merit rather than birth, was formally established during the Sui and Tang dynasties around the 7th century and lasted until it was abolished in 1905. It's considered one of the earliest large-scale meritocratic bureaucracies in world history, and versions of its written-exam model influenced civil service systems in Europe and beyond.

components.note: 咸 (all, together) — 感 relates to a shared reaction.
心 (heart) — feelings that stir the heart gave 感 its meaning 'to feel' or 'emotion.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 这是一个非常感人的故事。
example.pinyin: zhè shì yí gè fēicháng gǎnrén de gùshi.
example.english: This is a very touching story.
example.fact: Oxytocin, sometimes nicknamed the "bonding hormone," is released in the brain during moments of physical closeness like hugging or reunion, and it appears to strengthen feelings of trust and attachment between people. Studies have found oxytocin levels rise not just during physical contact but even while watching emotionally moving scenes, such as a tearful reunion in a film.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 培 originally described banking up soil around a plant's roots, extending to 'to cultivate, nurture.'
咅 (pǒu) gives a sound distantly related to péi, having drifted apart over time.
讠 (speech) — 训 relates to teaching through spoken instruction.
川 (chuān) gives a sound distantly related to xùn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 新员工要先完成一周的培训。
example.pinyin: xīn yuángōng yào xiān wánchéng yì zhōu de péixùn.
example.english: New employees must first complete a week of training.
example.fact: Medieval craft guilds in Europe typically required apprentices to train under a master for around seven years before they could even attempt the "masterpiece" exam needed to become a master craftsman themselves. The system was so central to how skills were passed on that many guilds tightly controlled how many apprentices any master could train at once, to protect the value of the trade.

components.note: 亻 (person) — relates to 传's meaning 'to pass on, transmit,' something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 传 is pronounced chuán, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — 球 originally referred to a round piece of jade, extended to mean 'ball, sphere'
求 (qiú) gives the sound — 球 is also pronounced qiú, an exact match

example.hanzi: 队员们互相传球，配合得很好。
example.pinyin: duìyuánmen hùxiāng chuánqiú, pèihé de hěn hǎo.
example.english: The teammates passed the ball to each other and worked together well.
example.fact: Basketball was invented in 1891 by physical education teacher James Naismith, who nailed two peach baskets to a gymnasium balcony and used a soccer ball, since basketballs themselves didn't exist yet. Because the baskets had solid bottoms at first, someone had to climb a ladder to retrieve the ball after every score until the open-bottomed hoop was introduced years later.

components.note: 六 is traditionally read as a simplified picture of a small hut or shelter with a peaked roof; the shape was later borrowed purely for its sound to represent the number six, unrelated to its original meaning.
灬 (fire) — 点 originally related to a small flame or dot of light, giving rise to the meaning 'dot' or 'point.'
占 (zhàn) gives a hint of the sound — 点 is pronounced diǎn, a connection that has drifted over the centuries.

example.hanzi: 我们六点在门口见面吧。
example.pinyin: wǒmen liùdiǎn zài ménkǒu jiànmiàn ba.
example.english: Let's meet at the entrance at six o'clock.
example.fact: Before the adoption of standardized time zones, every town commonly kept its own local solar time, so "six o'clock" could differ by minutes between neighboring cities — a serious problem once railway schedules connected them. The 1884 International Meridian Conference fixed this by establishing 24 worldwide time zones measured from the Greenwich meridian, the system still in use today.

components.note: 角 (horn) — 解 pictures removing a part of an animal.
牛 (ox) — together with a knife cutting between horn and ox, 解 pictures separating something into parts, giving its meaning 'to untie' or 'to explain.'
攵 (a hand taking action) — 救 describes the act of rescuing someone.
求 (qiú) gives a sound close to jiù, sharing a similar rhyme.

example.hanzi: 消防员及时解救了被困的孩子。
example.pinyin: xiāofángyuán jíshí jiějiù le bèi kùn de háizi.
example.english: The firefighters rescued the trapped child in time.
example.fact: In 2010, 33 Chilean miners survived 69 days trapped nearly 700 meters underground after a collapse at the San José mine, communicating with rescuers through a narrow borehole before all being pulled to the surface one by one in a specially built capsule named Fénix 2. The rescue was broadcast live and watched by an estimated one billion people worldwide.

components.note: A simplified pictograph of a bird's wings spread in flight — the source of 飞's meaning 'to fly.'
彳 (step/walk) — relates directly to 往's meaning 'to go toward, in the direction of.'
王 (wáng) gives a sound hint — 往 is pronounced wǎng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 这架航班将飞往东京。
example.pinyin: zhè jià hángbān jiāng fēiwǎng Dōngjīng.
example.english: This flight will fly to Tokyo.
example.fact: The longest nonstop commercial flight in the world, Singapore Airlines' route from Singapore to New York, covers roughly 15,300 kilometers and takes about 18 hours in the air. Because ultra-long-haul flights like this carry so much fuel, airlines must carefully calculate weight trade-offs between fuel, passengers, and cargo before the plane can even take off.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.
石 (rock) — 碎 describes something, often stone-like, broken into pieces.
卒 (zú) is only distantly related in sound to suì — the connection has drifted apart considerably over time.

example.hanzi: 花瓶不小心被打碎了。
example.pinyin: huāpíng bù xiǎoxīn bèi dǎsuì le.
example.english: The vase was accidentally smashed.
example.fact: Tempered glass, used in car windows and phone screens, is manufactured by rapidly cooling the surface of hot glass while the interior cools more slowly, locking in internal stresses. When that engineered stress is finally broken, the glass shatters all at once into small, relatively blunt pebble-like pieces rather than sharp shards, which is why it's considered safer than ordinary glass.

components.note: A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'
卫 simplifies 衛, which pictured feet (行) patrolling in a circuit around a walled settlement (韋) — soldiers making their rounds to protect it, the source of 卫's meaning 'to guard, defend.'

example.hanzi: 她学习柔道是为了自卫。
example.pinyin: tā xuéxí Róudào shì wèile zìwèi.
example.english: She's learning judo for self-defense.
example.fact: A skunk's primary self-defense mechanism is a foul-smelling musk sprayed from glands near its tail, which it can aim accurately at a threat's face from as far as three meters away. Skunks typically give a warning display — stamping their feet and arching their back — before spraying, since they only carry enough musk for a few uses before needing time to replenish it.

components.note: 辶 (to walk, movement) — 通 relates to passing through or getting somewhere.
甬 (yǒng) gives a hint of the sound — 通 is pronounced tōng, a connection that has shifted over time.

向 is traditionally read as a picture of a house with a window or vent in its roof, facing a particular way to let smoke or air escape — an orientation that gave the character its meaning 'toward, direction.'

example.hanzi: 这条小路通向山顶。
example.pinyin: zhè tiáo xiǎolù tōngxiàng shāndǐng.
example.english: This trail leads to the mountaintop.
example.fact: At its height, the Roman road network stretched more than 400,000 kilometers, with about 80,000 kilometers paved, connecting the empire from Britain to the Middle East. Well-built Roman roads used layered foundations of gravel and stone and were engineered with a slight curve to shed rainwater, a design so effective that some sections are still visible today.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 海 relates to bodies of water, specifically the sea.
每 (měi) gives a hint of the sound — 海 is pronounced hǎi, a connection that has shifted over time.
扌 (hand) — 报 relates to taking action against someone.
卩 (a kneeling or bound person) — handling a wrongdoer and announcing the judgment gave 报 its meaning 'to report' or 'to announce.'

example.hanzi: 墙上贴着一张电影海报。
example.pinyin: qiáng shàng tiē zhe yì zhāng diànyǐng hǎibào.
example.english: There's a movie poster stuck on the wall.
example.fact: The British government designed the "Keep Calm and Carry On" poster in 1939 to be distributed only if Nazi Germany invaded, so the vast majority of the roughly 2.5 million printed copies were pulped for paper and never displayed. A single surviving copy was rediscovered in a secondhand bookshop in 2000, sparking the design's worldwide popularity decades after it was created.

components.note: 言 (speech) — 警 relates to speaking out a warning or alarm
敬 (jìng) gives a sound close to 警's reading jǐng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
戈 (a spear) in the center is the weapon being wielded.
廾 (two hands) surrounding it show hands gripping the weapon on guard, giving 戒 its meaning 'to guard against, to warn.'

example.hanzi: 边境部队一直保持高度警戒。
example.pinyin: biānjìng bùduì yìzhí bǎochí gāodù jǐngjiè.
example.english: The border troops remain on high alert at all times.
example.fact: A honeybee colony always keeps a rotating shift of guard bees stationed at the hive entrance, using scent to check whether returning bees belong to the colony before letting them in. Guard bees that detect an intruder release an alarm pheromone that recruits other bees to help repel the threat within seconds.

components.note: 门 (door) frames the scene.
人 (person) glimpsed briefly inside, giving 闪 its meaning 'to flash, to dodge quickly.'
亮 is traditionally read as a picture of a lit oil lamp raised on a stand, radiating light — a fitting image for its meaning 'bright, radiant.'

example.hanzi: 星星在夜空中闪亮。
example.pinyin: xīngxīng zài yèkōng zhōng shǎnliàng.
example.english: The stars shine brightly in the night sky.
example.fact: Fireflies produce light through a chemical reaction between a molecule called luciferin and the enzyme luciferase, converting chemical energy into light with almost no heat lost — a conversion efficiency that puts even LED bulbs to shame. Each firefly species tends to have its own distinct flash pattern, which males and females use to recognize potential mates in the dark.

components.note: 页 (head) is the semantic root here, though the exact link to 顺's meaning 'to follow' isn't fully clear today.
川 (chuān) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading shùn has diverged.

着 developed from 著, whose upper part 草 (grass, plants) sits above 者 (a person) — plants settling onto and clinging to the ground gave 着 its core sense of 'attaching, resting on,' later grammaticalized into the particle marking an ongoing state.

example.hanzi: 顺着这条河往下游走，就能到达大海。
example.pinyin: shùnzhe zhè tiáo hé wǎng xiàyóu zǒu, jiù néng dàodá dàhǎi.
example.english: Follow this river downstream and you'll reach the sea.
example.fact: Salmon famously swim back up the same river system where they were born to spawn, navigating using a combination of the Earth's magnetic field for large-scale orientation and their sense of smell to recognize the precise chemical signature of their home stream once they get close. Some populations travel over 1,000 kilometers upstream against the current to complete the journey.

components.note: 犭 (dog) shows 猎 relates to hunting with animals.
昔 (xī) gives a sound distantly related to liè, having drifted apart over time.
牛 (ox/cattle) — cattle were among the earliest and most valuable kinds of property, connecting 物 to the general idea of 'object' or 'thing.'
勿 (wù) gives the sound — 物 is also pronounced wù, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 猎豹的速度让猎物几乎无法逃脱。
example.pinyin: lièbào de sùdù ràng lièwù jīhū wúfǎ táotuō.
example.english: The cheetah's speed leaves its prey almost no chance of escape.
example.fact: Cheetahs can accelerate from 0 to about 100 km/h in under three seconds and reach top speeds of roughly 100 to 120 km/h, making them the fastest land animal — but they can only sustain that sprint for around 20 to 30 seconds before overheating. Because of this, a hunt usually fails if the prey manages to stay just out of reach that long.

meanings: (used in complaining about sth) to be a nuisance

components.note: 女 (woman) with 覀 depicting hands on the waist — an old image of insisting or demanding something, connected to 要's meaning 'to want, to need.'
令 (an order, command) — 命 pictures issuing a command.
口 (mouth) — a command given aloud gave 命 its meaning 'order' or 'decree,' and by extension, 'fate' or 'life.'

example.hanzi: 今天热得要命。
example.pinyin: jīntiān rè de yàomìng.
example.english: It's unbearably hot today.
example.fact: The highest air temperature ever reliably recorded on Earth's surface was 56.7°C (134°F), measured in Death Valley, California, in July 2013. Death Valley's extreme heat comes partly from its shape: a long, narrow basin below sea level that traps and compresses descending hot air.

components.note: The upper part, related to 土, traditionally depicted one person's fate.
干 depicted a contrasting fate — the character set two outcomes side by side, with the fortunate one giving 幸 its meaning 'lucky, fortunate.'
子 (child/seed) — 存's meaning 'to exist, survive' has been linked to a seed persisting to grow.
才 (cái) gives a sound hint — 存 is pronounced cún, sharing the initial consonant though the vowel and tone differ.

example.hanzi: 那场事故中只有三个人幸存。
example.pinyin: nà chǎng shìgù zhōng zhǐyǒu sān gè rén xìngcún.
example.english: Only three people survived that accident.
example.fact: Of the roughly 2,224 passengers and crew aboard the Titanic when it sank in 1912, only about 706 survived, largely because the ship carried lifeboat capacity for barely half of everyone on board. The disaster led directly to international maritime law requiring ships to carry enough lifeboats for every person aboard, a rule still in force today.

components.note: 十 is thought to derive from a single knot tied partway along a length of rope — an ancient tally method in which one knot marked a count of ten.
五 places an X-shaped cross between two horizontal lines representing heaven and earth — in traditional cosmology, this was linked to the five elements that fill the space between.

example.hanzi: 教室里一共坐了十五个学生。
example.pinyin: jiàoshì lǐ yígòng zuò le shíwǔ gè xuésheng.
example.english: There are fifteen students sitting in the classroom in total.
example.fact: The Moon takes about 29.5 days to cycle through its phases from new moon to new moon, so the full moon reliably falls near the midpoint of that cycle, around day fourteen or fifteen. That timing depends on the Moon being on the exact opposite side of Earth from the Sun, fully lit as seen from the ground.

components.note: 犭 (dog) — 犯 originally related to a dog attacking, later extended to any act of violation
㔾 (jié) gives a sound distantly related to 犯's reading fàn, having drifted apart over time
见 (to see) — 规 originally named a craftsman's compass, a tool used to observe and measure circles, extended to 'rule, regulation.'
夫 (fū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from guī.

example.hanzi: 那名球员因犯规被罚下场。
example.pinyin: nà míng qiúyuán yīn fànguī bèi fá xiàchǎng.
example.english: That player was sent off for committing a foul.
example.fact: The NBA introduced the 24-second shot clock in 1954 after a nearly unwatchable 1950 game ended 19-18, with the leading team simply holding the ball and forcing fouls to run out the clock. The shot clock forced teams to attempt a shot within the time limit, transforming the pace and strategy of professional basketball almost overnight.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — 常 originally referred to a long skirt or banner made of cloth, later coming to mean something 'usual' or 'ordinary.'
尚 (shàng) gives a hint of the sound — 常 is pronounced cháng, a connection that has drifted over time.
见 (to see) — 规 originally named a craftsman's compass, a tool used to observe and measure circles, extended to 'rule, regulation.'
夫 (fū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from guī.

example.hanzi: 医生建议她做一次常规体检。
example.pinyin: yīshēng jiànyì tā zuò yí cì chángguī tǐjiǎn.
example.english: The doctor recommended she have a routine physical checkup.
example.fact: The commonly cited "normal" human body temperature of 37°C (98.6°F) comes from an 1868 study by German physician Carl Wunderlich, who compiled over a million temperature readings from thousands of patients. Modern research suggests average body temperature has actually drifted slightly lower since then, though 37°C remains the standard reference point in routine medical care.

components.note: 己 (a kneeling child) — the one being disciplined.
攵 (a hand with a stick) — correcting the child, giving 改 its meaning 'to change, correct, reform.'
羊 (sheep) — food offered generously to another person
口 (mouth) — kind words spoken alongside the gift

example.hanzi: 新政策大大改善了居民的生活条件。
example.pinyin: xīn zhèngcè dàdà gǎishàn le jūmín de shēnghuó tiáojiàn.
example.english: The new policy greatly improved residents' living conditions.
example.fact: Toyota's production philosophy of "kaizen," or continuous incremental improvement, encourages every worker on the assembly line — not just managers — to stop production and suggest fixes the moment they spot a problem. The approach, developed in Japan after World War II, became a foundation of modern lean manufacturing practiced by companies worldwide.

components.note: 酉 (a wine jar) — the vessel holding the drink
氵 (liquid) — the wine itself inside the jar

后 merges two originally separate characters: an old pictograph of a ruler issuing commands (the source of meanings like 'queen'), and 後, which combined 彳 (to walk) with a trailing thread and a foot to depict someone lagging behind — the source of 后's modern meaning 'after, behind.'

example.hanzi: 酒后驾车是非常危险的行为。
example.pinyin: jiǔhòu jiàchē shì fēicháng wēixiǎn de xíngwéi.
example.english: Driving after drinking is an extremely dangerous behavior.
example.fact: The first practical breathalyzer, developed by American police captain and biochemist Robert Borkenstein in 1954, measured blood alcohol content by having a driver breathe into a balloon connected to a chemical solution that changed color in proportion to alcohol concentration. His device gave law enforcement a fast, roadside way to estimate impairment for the first time, replacing earlier tests that required a hospital blood draw.
